mainTopic: The required wording and endings of ברכת המזון, the rule אין חותמין בשתים, and the make-up blessings for forgetting שבת, יום טוב, or ראש חודש
overview: This amud deals with the exact wording of ברכת המזון. It finishes a ברייתא: ברית is mentioned before תורה, רבי אבא requires הודאה at the start and end of ברכת הארץ, and leaving out ברית, תורה, or מלכות בית דוד means one has not fulfilled the obligation. The גמרא brings a dispute over whether הטוב והמטיב needs מלכות, which depends on whether that ברכה is דאורייתא or דרבנן. It then asks how to end בונה ירושלים. רב חסדא objects to ending with two themes, citing רבי's rule אין חותמין בשתים. That rule is tested against several endings and explained by the principle that מצוות are not done in bundles. רב ששת and רב נחמן then disagree about the proper ending. In a story, רב חסדא is criticized for following רב's lone view that ברית, תורה, and מלכות may be left out. The גמרא next explains why הטוב והמטיב contains extra mentions of מלכות. Finally, רב גידל teaches the make-up blessings for someone who forgot שבת, יום טוב, or ראש חודש, and a new story about רב נחמן's mistake begins, continuing on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the covenant of circumcision comes before Torah
steps.stepSummary: Completes the reasoning (begun on the previous page) for mentioning ברית before תורה: ברית מילה was given with thirteen covenants.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this one (circumcision) was given with thirteen covenants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a sentence from the previous page. It gives the reason why ברית (circumcision) should be mentioned before תורה in ברכת הארץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full ברייתא line reads: 'This one (תורה) was given with three covenants, and this one (מילה) was given with thirteen covenants.' The word ברית appears thirteen times in the circumcision section with אברהם (בראשית יז). Because מילה has more covenants, it is mentioned first.

keyTerms.meaning: Covenants; here, the thirteen times the word ברית appears in the passage about מילה

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the second half of a sentence that started on the previous page. 'And this one' means מילה, compared to תורה, which was given with only three covenants.

phrases.english: And this one (circumcision) was given
phrases.notes: This is set against the תורה, mentioned just before, which was given with three covenants.

phrases.english: with thirteen covenants.
phrases.notes: The word ברית appears 13 times in בראשית יז

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reasoning for the order of ברית before תורה, begun earlier
steps.raayaObject: The rule that ברית must be mentioned before תורה in ברכת הארץ
steps.raayaSupportSource: The thirteen mentions of ברית in the circumcision passage (בראשית יז)

steps.title: Thanks must open and close the blessing of the land
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא rules that ברכת הארץ must contain הודאה at its start and its end. Someone who shortens it must keep at least one, and keeping none is disgraceful.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא says: One must say thanks in it at the beginning and at the end. One who shortens should not go below one. Anyone who goes below one is acting disgracefully.
steps.whatsHappening: A new opinion in the ברייתא: רבי אבא explains how 'thanks' (הודאה) must appear in ברכת הארץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ברכת הארץ is a blessing of thanks. So it should open with thanks ('נודה לך') and close with thanks ('ועל הכל אנחנו מודים לך'). If a person shortens the blessing, he may drop one of these, but never both. Leaving out all thanks is called מגונה, disgraceful.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba says:
One must say thanks in it
phrases.notes: 'It' means ברכת הארץ, the blessing of thanks for the land

phrases.english: at the beginning and the end.
And one who shortens should not go below one.
And anyone who goes below one —
this is disgraceful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new requirement for ברכת הארץ, alongside the earlier rules about ברית and תורה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ברכת הארץ needs הודאה at the beginning and end. At minimum one הודאה is required, and fewer is מגונה.

steps.title: Wrong endings make a person an ignoramus
steps.stepSummary: Ending ברכת הארץ with 'מנחיל ארצות' or ending בונה ירושלים with 'מושיע ישראל' marks a person as a בור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Anyone who ends the blessing of the land with 'Who bequeaths lands', and ends 'Who builds Jerusalem' with 'Who saves Israel', is an ignoramus.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now discusses the closing line (חתימה) of two blessings. It lists endings that are wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each blessing's ending must match its topic. 'מנחיל ארצות' (plural lands) does not fit thanks for ארץ ישראל specifically. 'מושיע ישראל' does not fit a blessing about rebuilding ירושלים. Someone who changes these endings shows he does not understand the blessing, so he is called a בור.

keyTerms.meaning: Who bequeaths lands; an incorrect ending
Who saves Israel; an incorrect ending here

steps.confusionAlert: The בור label is about the wording being wrong. It is different from the next line, which says 'לא יצא' (he did not fulfill his obligation). These are two different levels of problem.

phrases.english: And anyone who concludes with 'Who bequeaths lands'
in the blessing of the land,
and with 'Who saves Israel'
in 'Who builds Jerusalem' —
this one is an ignoramus.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the body of ברכת הארץ to the closing formulas of ברכת הארץ and בונה ירושלים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ending ברכת הארץ with 'מנחיל ארצות' or בונה ירושלים with 'מושיע ישראל' marks one as a בור.

steps.title: Missing covenant, Torah, or David's kingship means no fulfillment
steps.stepSummary: If one leaves out ברית and תורה from ברכת הארץ, or מלכות בית דוד from בונה ירושלים, he has not fulfilled his obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: And anyone who does not say 'covenant' and 'Torah' in the blessing of the land, and 'the kingship of the house of David' in 'Who builds Jerusalem', has not fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא lists required content. Leaving it out means the blessing does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is stronger than the בור label. Mentioning ברית and תורה is part of the core of ברכת הארץ, and the kingship of דוד is part of the core of בונה ירושלים. Without them, the person has not fulfilled his obligation (לא יצא ידי חובתו).

keyTerms.meaning: The kingship of the house of David
He has not fulfilled his obligation

steps.whatToRemember: ברכת הארץ must mention ברית and תורה. בונה ירושלים must mention מלכות בית דוד. Without these, ברכת המזון is not fulfilled.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical source for why our ברכת המזון says 'ועל בריתך... ועל תורתך' and 'ועל מלכות בית דוד משיחך'.

phrases.english: And anyone who does not say 'covenant' and 'Torah'
in the blessing of the land,
and 'the kingship of the house of David'
in 'Who builds Jerusalem' —
has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל שֶׁאֵינוֹ אוֹמֵר בְּרִית וְתוֹרָה בְּבִרְכַּת הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from wrong endings (בור) to missing core content (לא יצא)
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Omitting ברית and תורה from ברכת הארץ, or מלכות בית דוד from בונה ירושלים, means one has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.title: The ברייתא supports רבי אילעא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the ברייתא's last ruling supports רבי אילעא, who quoted the same rule in the name of רבינו.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רבי אילעא. For רבי אילעא said in the name of רבי יעקב בר אחא, in the name of our teacher (רבינו): Anyone who did not say 'covenant' and 'Torah' in the blessing of the land, and 'the kingship of the house of David' in 'Who builds Jerusalem', has not fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now speaks in its own voice. It points out that the ברייתא just quoted backs up an אמורא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אילעא reported, through רבי יעקב בר אחא, a ruling from רבינו (רבי יהודה הנשיא). The ruling matches the ברייתא word for word. The phrase מסייע ליה tells us the ברייתא is a supporting source for that teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: Our teacher; here רבי יהודה הנשיא

steps.confusionAlert: The quote from רבי אילעא repeats the ברייתא's words on purpose. The point is to show that the two sources match, so this is not a new rule.
steps.whatToRemember: The requirement to mention ברית, תורה, and מלכות בית דוד comes from both a ברייתא and רבי's own teaching.

phrases.english: This supports Rabbi Il'a,
as Rabbi Il'a said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אַחָא מִשּׁוּם רַבֵּינוּ:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Ya'akov bar Acha said in the name of our teacher:
phrases.notes: 'Our teacher' here means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: Anyone who did not say 'covenant' and 'Torah'
in the blessing of the land
and 'the kingship of the house of David'
in 'Who builds Jerusalem' —
has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links the ברייתא's ruling in step 4 to an אמורא's matching teaching
steps.raayaObject: רבי אילעא's ruling (in the name of רבינו) that omitting ברית, תורה, or מלכות בית דוד invalidates ברכת המזון
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's line 'וכל שאינו אומר ברית ותורה... לא יצא ידי חובתו'

steps.title: A dispute over whether הטוב והמטיב needs מלכות
steps.stepSummary: אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי and the רבנן disagree whether the fourth ברכה of ברכת המזון, הטוב והמטיב, must mention God's kingship.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי and the רבנן argue about this. One says הטוב והמטיב needs a mention of God as King. The other says it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new dispute about the fourth ברכה of ברכת המזון: must it say 'מלך העולם' or not?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sides are stated without saying which person holds which view (חד אמר... וחד אמר). The question is whether הטוב והמטיב must include the standard kingship phrase. The reasons for each view come in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Who is good and does good' – the fourth ברכה of ברכת המזון
kingship – mentioning God as 'King of the world' in a ברכה
one said... and the other said (the views are not assigned to specific people)

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ אַבָּא יוֹסֵי בֶּן דּוֹסְתַּאי וְרַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: Abba Yosei ben Dostai and the Rabbis disagree about it.
One said: 'Who is good and does good' requires mention of kingship,
and one said: It does not require mention of kingship.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ אַבָּא יוֹסֵי בֶּן דּוֹסְתַּאי וְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the second and third ברכות (ברכת הארץ, בונה ירושלים) to the fourth ברכה, הטוב והמטיב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מחלוקת over whether הטוב והמטיב requires מלכות.

steps.title: The reason behind each side
steps.stepSummary: Whoever requires מלכות holds that הטוב והמטיב is דרבנן. Whoever does not require it holds that it is דאורייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says it needs kingship holds that this ברכה was made by the Rabbis. The one who says it does not need kingship holds that it comes from the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why each side holds as it does. It ties the dispute to whether הטוב והמטיב comes from the Torah or from the Rabbis.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If הטוב והמטיב is דרבנן, it was added later as its own separate ברכה, so it must open with its own mention of God's kingship. If it is דאורייתא, it counts as part of the Torah's original ברכת המזון. It then continues the earlier ברכות and does not need its own מלכות.

keyTerms.meaning: a rabbinic law (added by the Sages)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that wording rules for a ברכה can depend on that ברכה's source: whether it is part of the original Torah structure or a later rabbinic addition.

phrases.english: The one who says it requires kingship
holds that it is rabbinic.
And the one who says it does not require kingship
holds that it is from the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר צְרִיכָה מַלְכוּת קָסָבַר דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning of both views in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Requiring מלכות goes with הטוב והמטיב being דרבנן (a separate ברכה). Not requiring it goes with its being דאורייתא (part of the original ברכות).

steps.title: A ברייתא on how to end בונה ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks how one ends the ברכה about rebuilding Jerusalem. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה answers: 'מושיע ישראל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: How does one end the ברכה about building Jerusalem? רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: 'Who saves Israel.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about the closing words of the third ברכה, בונה ירושלים. It is setting up a difficulty the גמרא will raise next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read literally, רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה gives only one ending, מושיע ישראל. That seems strange, because the ברכה is about Jerusalem and normally ends 'בונה ירושלים'.

keyTerms.meaning: ends / concludes the ברכה with its closing line
the building of Jerusalem (the third ברכה)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
With what does one conclude the blessing of the building of Jerusalem?

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: ״מוֹשִׁיעַ יִשְׂרָאֵל״.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says: 'Who saves Israel.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַהוּ חוֹתֵם בְּבִנְיַן יְרוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the third ברכה, which was discussed in steps 3–4 (where ending בונה ירושלים with מושיע ישראל was called the mark of a בור).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, בונה ירושלים may end with 'מושיע ישראל'.

steps.title: Does that mean 'בונה ירושלים' is not allowed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: does רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה mean that only מושיע ישראל works, and the natural ending בונה ירושלים does not?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Who saves Israel' – yes, but 'Who builds Jerusalem' – no?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the plain reading of the ברייתא. It finds it hard to believe that one may not end a Jerusalem ברכה with 'בונה ירושלים'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברכה is about Jerusalem, so 'בונה ירושלים' is the obvious ending. A reading that permits only מושיע ישראל would rule out the most natural ending, which cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Who builds Jerusalem' – the standard ending of the third ברכה

phrases.english: 'Who saves Israel' – yes,
'Who builds Jerusalem' – no?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the plain reading of the ברייתא in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plain reading of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, that the ending is only מושיע ישראל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברכה about Jerusalem cannot reasonably exclude the ending 'בונה ירושלים'.

steps.title: Read it as 'also' מושיע ישראל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא: one ends with בונה ירושלים, and one may also end with מושיע ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: even 'Who saves Israel' is acceptable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the reading of the ברייתא by adding the word 'אף' (even/also).
steps.deeperAnalysis: בונה ירושלים remains the basic ending. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה only adds that מושיע ישראל is also acceptable. This removes the difficulty from step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: rather, say (read the source this way)

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean one ends with both phrases together. It means either ending is acceptable. Ending with two themes together is exactly what the next part of the גמרא questions.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
Even 'Who saves Israel.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to allow only מושיע ישראל.
steps.terutzMaskana: בונה ירושלים is the main ending, and מושיע ישראל is also acceptable.

steps.title: רבה בר רב הונא ends with two themes
steps.stepSummary: At the house of the ריש גלותא, רבה בר רב הונא opened the ברכה with one theme and closed it with two.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא happened to come to the house of the ריש גלותא. He opened with one theme and concluded with two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about how someone actually said this ברכה. It sets up a challenge that follows right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Based on the 'אף' reading, רבה בר רב הונא seems to have combined both endings, 'מושיע ישראל ובונה ירושלים', even though the body of the ברכה dealt with one theme. The question is whether combining two endings is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: the Exilarch, head of the Jewish community in Babylonia

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna
happened to come to the house of the Exilarch.
He opened with one and concluded with two.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows a real case of ending with both מושיע ישראל and בונה ירושלים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה בר רב הונא concluded the Jerusalem ברכה with two themes.

steps.title: רב חסדא objects: one may not end with two
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא mocks the double ending and cites a ברייתא in which רבי rules that one may not end a ברכה with two themes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: What a feat, to conclude with two! But it was taught: רבי says one may not conclude with two!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא challenges what רבה בר רב הונא did, using a ברייתא of רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each ברכה should end with one clear theme. רבי's rule 'אין חותמין בשתים' seems to directly forbid the double ending of step 11. The גמרא first examines רבי's rule itself (steps 13–27). It then returns to how this ברכה should end (steps 28–30).

keyTerms.meaning: but was it not taught in a ברייתא?
one does not end a ברכה with two themes

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
What a feat, to conclude with two!
But was it not taught:
Rabbi says: One may not conclude with two!

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּבוּרְתָּא לְמֶחְתַּם בְּתַרְתֵּי! וְהָתַנְיָא רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: אֵין חוֹתְמִין בִּשְׁתַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the practice described in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר רב הונא's double ending.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי's ברייתא forbids ending a ברכה with two themes.

steps.title: Looking at רבי's rule on its own
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pauses with 'גופא' to examine רבי's rule 'אין חותמין בשתים' directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: רבי says, one may not conclude with two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רבי's rule so it can examine it more closely. This step sets up the challenges that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'גופא' signals that a source quoted in passing will now be studied for its own sake. Next, לוי tests the rule against standard ברכה endings that seem to contain two themes.

keyTerms.meaning: 'the matter itself' – the גמרא returns to examine a quoted source directly

phrases.english: The matter itself.
Rabbi says: One may not conclude with two.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא. רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: אֵין חוֹתְמִין בִּשְׁתַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the ברייתא cited in step 12 and makes it the new subject of discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ברכה may not be concluded with two themes.

steps.title: לוי: 'על הארץ ועל המזון' has two themes
steps.stepSummary: לוי challenges רבי with the ending of ברכת הארץ, which seems to mention two things: the land and the food.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי objected to רבי: But we say 'For the land and for the food'!
steps.whatsHappening: לוי points to a well-known ברכה ending that seems to break רבי's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second ברכה of ברכת המזון ends 'על הארץ ועל המזון'. That looks like two separate themes, which would contradict 'אין חותמין בשתים'.

keyTerms.meaning: he raised an objection against him
'for the land and for the food' – the ending of ברכת הארץ

phrases.english: Levi raised an objection to Rabbi:
'For the land and for the food'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ לֵוִי לְרַבִּי, ״עַל הָאָרֶץ וְעַל הַמָּזוֹן״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule stated in step 13.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An accepted ברכה ending seems to contain two themes, land and food.

steps.title: It is one theme: land that produces food
steps.stepSummary: רבי answers that 'land and food' is a single theme: the land that brings out food.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means a land that produces food.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי answers לוי by showing that the two words describe one idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ending thanks God for one thing: the land as the source of food. The food is not a separate topic, so the ending has only one theme and the rule stands.

phrases.english: A land that produces food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers לוי's objection in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the two words form one combined theme.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Land' and 'food' seemed to be two separate themes.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is one theme: the land as the producer of food.

steps.title: לוי again: 'על הארץ ועל הפירות'
steps.stepSummary: לוי raises a second example: the ending of the ברכה מעין שלש over fruit, 'על הארץ ועל הפירות'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we say 'For the land and for the fruit'!
steps.whatsHappening: לוי brings a second ending that seems to have two themes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of challenge, now from the ברכה said after eating fruits of the seven species (ברכה מעין שלש). Again, land and fruit look like two separate topics.

keyTerms.meaning: 'for the land and for the fruit' – the ending of the ברכה after fruits

phrases.english: 'For the land and for the fruit'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second objection of the same type as step 14.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another accepted ending seems to have two themes, land and fruit.

steps.title: Again one theme: land that produces fruit
steps.stepSummary: רבי answers the same way: it means the land that produces fruit, which is one theme.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means a land that produces fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי gives the same kind of answer as before: the land and its fruit are one idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ending that mentions two things that are really one combined idea (a source and what it produces) does not count as 'two'. רבי's rule survives both of לוי's challenges.
steps.whatToRemember: 'אין חותמין בשתים' forbids ending a ברכה with two truly separate themes. Two words that form one idea, such as 'the land that produces food/fruit', count as one theme.

phrases.english: A land that produces fruit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 16 the same way step 15 answered step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the two words form one combined theme.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Land' and 'fruit' seemed to be two themes.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is one theme: the land as the producer of fruit.

steps.title: לוי challenges with the יום טוב blessing ending
steps.stepSummary: לוי cites the יום טוב ending 'מקדש ישראל והזמנים', which seems to mention two things.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we say: 'Who sanctifies Israel and the seasons'!
steps.whatsHappening: לוי brings a third example against רבי. The ending of the יום טוב ברכה seems to name two separate things: Israel and the holidays.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a ברכה may not end with two themes, how can the standard יום טוב ending mention both ישראל and הזמנים? This follows the same pattern as לוי's earlier challenges about the land and food, and the land and fruit.

keyTerms.meaning: The appointed times, meaning the festivals (יום טוב)

phrases.english: "Who sanctifies Israel and the seasons"!
phrases.notes: The ending of the middle ברכה of קידוש and the עמידה on יום טוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues לוי's series of counterexamples after רבי answered the fruit case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A standard ending names two things (Israel and the holidays), so it seems to break the rule.

steps.title: Israel, who sanctify the holidays
steps.stepSummary: רבי explains that the ending means 'Israel, who make the holidays holy', which is one theme.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means: Israel, who sanctify the seasons.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי answers that the two words make up one idea. ה׳ sanctifies Israel, and Israel are the ones who sanctify the holidays.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The holidays get their holiness through Israel. The בית דין of Israel fixes the calendar, so the holiday dates depend on them. So 'Israel and the seasons' is one chain of holiness, not two separate praises. This is the same kind of answer רבי gave for 'the land that brings out food'.

phrases.english: Israel, who sanctified the seasons.
phrases.notes: Israel fixes the calendar through בית דין, so the holidays' holiness comes through them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers לוי's challenge in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the two-part phrase is read as one combined theme
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Israel and the holidays are two separate things being praised.
steps.terutzMaskana: ה׳ sanctifies Israel, who in turn sanctify the holidays. That is one theme.

steps.title: לוי challenges with the ראש חודש ending
steps.stepSummary: לוי cites the ראש חודש ending 'מקדש ישראל וראשי חדשים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we say: 'Who sanctifies Israel and the New Moons'!
steps.whatsHappening: לוי brings another ending that seems to have two parts: Israel and ראש חודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works just like the יום טוב challenge. The ending seems to name two separate holy things.

keyTerms.meaning: The New Moons, meaning ראש חודש days

phrases.english: "Who sanctifies Israel and the New Moons"!
phrases.notes: The ending of the ראש חודש ברכה in מוסף.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another counterexample in the same pattern as step 18.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ending names Israel and ראש חודש, which looks like two themes.

steps.title: Israel, who sanctify the New Moons
steps.stepSummary: רבי gives the same answer: Israel are the ones who sanctify ראש חודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means: Israel, who sanctify the New Moons.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי repeats his answer. The ending means one thing: ה׳ sanctifies Israel, who sanctify ראש חודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ראש חודש is declared by בית דין of Israel when witnesses see the new moon, so its holiness also flows through Israel. This again makes it a single theme.

keyTerms.meaning: The sanctifying of the new month by בית דין

phrases.english: Israel, who sanctified the New Moons.
phrases.notes: Refers to קידוש החודש by בית דין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20 the same way step 19 answered step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Israel and ראש חודש are two separate praises.
steps.terutzMaskana: Israel sanctify ראש חודש, so it is one theme.

steps.title: לוי challenges with the שבת-and-יום טוב ending
steps.stepSummary: לוי cites the ending used when שבת and יום טוב fall together: 'מקדש השבת וישראל והזמנים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we say: 'Who sanctifies the Shabbat, and Israel, and the seasons'!
steps.whatsHappening: לוי brings his strongest example. On a יום טוב that falls on שבת, the ending names שבת, Israel, and the holidays.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the earlier answer does not work. Israel do not make שבת holy, because שבת is holy on its own every seventh day. So שבת really does seem to be a separate theme next to 'Israel and the holidays'.

keyTerms.meaning: שבת, whose holiness is fixed by ה׳ and does not depend on Israel

phrases.english: "Who sanctifies the Shabbat, and Israel, and the seasons"!
phrases.notes: Said when יום טוב falls on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Escalates the challenge to a case that the 'Israel who sanctify' answer cannot cover.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שבת's holiness does not come through Israel, so this ending seems to have two truly separate themes.

steps.title: Except for this one
steps.stepSummary: רבי admits this ending is an exception to his rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Except for this one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי does not try to reread the words. He simply says this ending is an exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule still stands, but this ending is allowed even though it names more than one thing. Why it is allowed is not yet explained. The גמרא asks about that next.

phrases.english: Except for this one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 22 by granting an exception.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: This ending proves the rule is wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule stands. This ending is a special exception.

steps.title: Why is this ending different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the שבת-and-יום טוב ending is allowed when other two-theme endings are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is different?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why this ending gets an exception. This sets up the next step, which gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An exception needs a reason. The comparison is to the third ברכה of ברכת המזון, where ending with two themes is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? It asks for the reason behind a distinction.

phrases.english: And what is different?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind רבי's exception.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the שבת-and-יום טוב ending is allowed when the ברכת המזון case is not.

steps.title: One holiness of the day versus two separate themes
steps.stepSummary: Here the ending praises one thing, the holiness of the day. There, the two themes are each separate.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it is one thing. There it is two, each one standing by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the שבת-and-יום טוב ending is really about one thing: the holiness of this single day. In the third ברכה of ברכת המזון, building ירושלים and saving Israel are two separate topics.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though שבת and יום טוב are mentioned, the ברכה thanks ה׳ for one thing, the קדושת היום of today. In the other case, the two themes have nothing joining them, so it would be two ברכות squeezed into one.

keyTerms.meaning: There (the third ברכה of ברכת המזון)

steps.confusionAlert: 'התם' does not mean the יום טוב or ראש חודש endings. It points back to the ברכת המזון case, about ירושלים and the saving of Israel, where ending with two themes is not allowed.

phrases.english: Here it is one thing,
phrases.notes: The one thing is the holiness of the single day.

phrases.english: there it is two,
phrases.notes: The two things are building ירושלים and saving Israel.

phrases.english: each one by itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The שבת-and-יום טוב ending praises one thing, the holiness of the day. The ברכת המזון themes are two unconnected things.

steps.title: What is the reason for the rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a ברכה may not end with two themes in the first place.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason that we do not end a ברכה with two themes?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא steps back and asks for the reason behind רבי's rule itself. This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the discussion was about which endings count as one theme. Now the גמרא wants the principle behind the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: End or close a ברכה (the closing 'ברוך אתה' line)

phrases.english: And what is the reason
that we do not end with two?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the challenges are settled, the גמרא asks for the reason behind the rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason behind the rule אין חותמין בשתים.

steps.title: We do not do מצוות in bundles
steps.stepSummary: The reason: מצוות are not done in bundles. Each one deserves its own attention.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because we do not do מצוות in bundles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the rule comes from a general principle: we do not lump מצוות together. Each praise deserves its own ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Squeezing two separate praises into one ending treats them like a package deal. That looks like we want to get them over with. Giving each its own ending shows proper respect.

keyTerms.meaning: In bundles, meaning lumping several things together
The principle that מצוות should not be done as a bundle

steps.whatToRemember: A ברכה may end with one theme only (אין חותמין בשתים). Two-part endings like 'the land and the food' or 'Israel and the holidays' are allowed because they are really one theme. The שבת-and-יום טוב ending is allowed because it praises the single holiness of the day. The reason for the rule is אין עושין מצוות חבילות חבילות.
steps.whyThisMatters: The principle that מצוות are not done in bundles shows up across ש״ס, for example in rules about not combining two celebrations or two מצוות at once.

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין עוֹשִׂין מִצְוֹת חֲבִילוֹת חֲבִילוֹת.
phrases.english: Because we do not perform מצוות in bundles.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין עוֹשִׂין מִצְוֹת חֲבִילוֹת חֲבִילוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule comes from the principle אין עושין מצוות חבילות חבילות.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Each separate praise needs its own ending, because מצוות should not be bundled together.

steps.title: What is the final ruling on the Jerusalem ending?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the final ruling is on how to end the third ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was decided about it?
steps.whatsHappening: The earlier discussion left the ending of the third ברכה unsettled, so the גמרא asks for the bottom line. It is setting up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous steps explained that a ברכה should not end with two separate themes. So the question is which single theme ends this ברכה: Israel or ירושלים.

phrases.english: What was concluded about it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the unresolved question from steps 8–12 (how to end בונה ירושלים, given רבה בר רב הונא's double ending) and asks for the practical ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The correct ending (חתימה) of the third ברכה of ברכת המזון.

steps.title: The ending matches the opening
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says the ending depends on how the ברכה opened.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: If he opened with 'Have mercy on Your people Israel,' he ends with 'Who saves Israel.' If he opened with 'Have mercy on Jerusalem,' he ends with 'Who builds Jerusalem.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers that the ending should match the opening. If you started with Israel, end with Israel. If you started with ירושלים, end with ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This avoids a two-theme ending. Each version of the ברכה keeps one consistent theme from start to finish.

keyTerms.meaning: He opened (the beginning of the ברכה)
He ends / seals (the closing line of the ברכה)

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
If he opened with 'Have mercy on Your people Israel'
he ends with 'Who saves Israel.'
If he opened with 'Have mercy on Jerusalem'
he ends with 'Who builds Jerusalem.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ending follows the opening: Israel leads to מושיע ישראל, ירושלים leads to בונה ירושלים.

steps.title: Always end with Who builds Jerusalem
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says that even an Israel opening ends with בונה ירושלים, based on a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Even if he opened with 'Have mercy on Israel,' he ends with 'Who builds Jerusalem.' This is because the פסוק says, 'ה׳ builds Jerusalem, He gathers the scattered ones of Israel.' When does ה׳ build Jerusalem? At the time He gathers the scattered ones of Israel.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן disagrees with רב ששת. He says the ending is always בונה ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק ties the two ideas together: the building of ירושלים happens when Israel is gathered. So ending with ירושלים is not a different theme from Israel. It already includes Israel's rescue.

keyTerms.meaning: Because it is stated (introduces a פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: רב ששת matches the ending to the opening. רב נחמן always ends with בונה ירושלים, because building ירושלים means gathering Israel.
steps.whyThisMatters: Our text of ברכת המזון ends the third ברכה with בונה ירושלים, which fits רב נחמן's approach.

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman said:
Even if he opened with 'Have mercy on Israel'
he ends with 'Who builds Jerusalem,'
because it is stated:
'ה׳ builds Jerusalem, He gathers the scattered ones of Israel' (Tehillim 147:2):
When does ה׳ build Jerusalem?
At the time when He gathers the scattered ones of Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A disagreeing answer to the same question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The third ברכה always ends with בונה ירושלים, because ירושלים's rebuilding includes the gathering of Israel.

steps.title: רב חסדא refuses to teach
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks רב חסדא to teach, and רב חסדא says he has not even learned ברכת המזון properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to רב חסדא: Let the master come and teach. He answered: I have not learned ברכת המזון, and I should teach?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story on a related topic. It sets up the next question: why does רב חסדא say he does not know ברכת המזון?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא says this because of something that happened to him, which he explains in the next steps. The story will show which parts of ברכת המזון are required.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the master come and teach

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Rav Chisda:
Let the master come and teach.
He said to him:
I have not learned Grace after Meals,
and shall I teach?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new related story about the text of ברכת המזון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב חסדא claims he has not yet mastered ברכת המזון, so he is not fit to teach.

steps.title: What do you mean?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks what רב חסדא means.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What is this?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא is surprised and asks what רב חסדא means by saying he does not know ברכת המזון. It sets up the explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying ברכת המזון is something everyone does. So it is strange for a great scholar to say he has not learned it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is this? (What do you mean?)

phrases.english: He said to him: What is this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind רב חסדא's claim.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב חסדא says he has not learned ברכת המזון.

steps.title: רב ששת's angry reaction
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא tells how רב ששת got angry at his ברכת המזון in the house of the ריש גלותא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I happened to be at the house of the ריש גלותא, and I said ברכת המזון. רב ששת stiffened his neck at me like a snake.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא explains that רב ששת reacted angrily to the way he said ברכת המזון. This made him feel he had not learned it properly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Like a snake' is a picture of strong anger and challenge. We are not told the reason yet, so the next step asks why.

keyTerms.meaning: The Exilarch, leader of the Jews in Bavel

phrases.english: He said to him:
For I happened to come to the house of the Exilarch,
and I recited Grace after Meals,
and Rav Sheshet stiffened his neck
at me like a snake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב ששת got angry at how רב חסדא said ברכת המזון.

steps.title: Why was he angry?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks why רב ששת was angry.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא asks what רב חסדא did wrong. This sets up the explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story so far tells us there was a mistake, but not what it was. Knowing the mistake will show which parts of ברכת המזון are essential.

phrases.english: And why?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the reason for רב ששת's anger.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What omission or error caused רב ששת's anger.

steps.title: He left out covenant, Torah and kingship
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא did not mention ברית, תורה or מלכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because I did not say 'covenant,' nor 'Torah,' nor 'kingship.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא explains his mistake: he left out three themes, ברית, תורה and מלכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These themes belong in ברכת המזון, mainly in the ברכה about the land (ברית and תורה). רב ששת held that leaving them out is a real flaw.

keyTerms.meaning: Kingship (of בית דוד, or of ה׳)

phrases.english: Because I did not say

phrases.aramaic: לֹא בְּרִית וְלֹא תּוֹרָה וְלֹא מַלְכוּת.
phrases.english: not covenant, nor Torah, nor kingship.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּלָא אֲמַרִי לֹא בְּרִית וְלֹא תּוֹרָה וְלֹא מַלְכוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers why רב ששת was angry.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He left out ברית, תורה and מלכות.

steps.title: Why did you leave them out?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks why רב חסדא left out these themes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why did you not say them?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא asks what reason רב חסדא had for leaving them out. It sets up רב חסדא's source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא was a great scholar, so his omission was likely based on a source. The question draws that source out.

phrases.english: And why did you not say them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of the omission.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source רב חסדא relied on.

steps.title: Relying on רב: these themes are not required
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא followed רב, who said one still fulfills the obligation without ברית, תורה and מלכות, since they do not apply to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like רב חננאל said in the name of רב: If he did not say covenant, Torah and kingship, he has fulfilled his obligation. Covenant is left out because it does not apply to women. Torah and kingship are left out because they apply neither to women nor to slaves.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא says he relied on רב, who rules that leaving out these three themes does not ruin ברכת המזון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's logic is that ברכת המזון is said by everyone, including women and slaves. A theme that does not apply to all who say it cannot be an absolute requirement. Women have no ברית מילה, and women and slaves are not obligated in learning תורה and have no share in the kingship.

keyTerms.meaning: Because it does not apply to women
In line with the view of רב

phrases.english: In line with what Rav Chananel said in the name of Rav,
for Rav Chananel said in the name of Rav:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אָמַר בְּרִית וְתוֹרָה וּמַלְכוּת — יָצָא.
phrases.english: If he did not say covenant, Torah and kingship, he has fulfilled his obligation.
Covenant: because it does not apply to women.
Torah and kingship:

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵינָן לֹא בְּנָשִׁים וְלֹא בַּעֲבָדִים.
phrases.english: because they apply neither to women nor to slaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the omission.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב rules that one is יוצא without ברית, תורה and מלכות, since these do not apply to everyone who says ברכת המזון.

steps.title: You followed רב against everyone else?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא challenges רב חסדא for following רב against many תנאים and אמוראים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And you left all these תנאים and אמוראים and acted like רב?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא attacks רב חסדא's choice. Many authorities require these themes, so רב ששת was right to be angry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is not that רב has no reasoning. The problem is that רב is a lone view against the majority. In practice, one should not follow a single opinion against so many.

keyTerms.meaning: תנאים and אמוראים, the sages of the משנה and the גמרא

steps.whatToRemember: ברית, תורה and מלכות do belong in ברכת המזון. רב's lenient view was rejected because so many authorities disagree.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is why our ברכת המזון mentions בריתך and תורתך in the second ברכה, and the kingship of בית דוד in the third.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַתְּ שְׁבַקְתְּ כֹּל הָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי וְאָמוֹרָאֵי,
phrases.english: And you abandoned all these Tannaim and Amoraim,
and acted like Rav?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַתְּ שְׁבַקְתְּ כֹּל הָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי וְאָמוֹרָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב חסדא's reliance on רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's practice of following רב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A single view (רב) should not be followed against many תנאים and אמוראים who require these themes.

steps.title: הטוב והמטיב needs מלכות
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the ברכה of הטוב והמטיב must mention מלכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: 'Who is good and does good' needs kingship.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement: the fourth ברכה, הטוב והמטיב, must include a mention of ה׳ as King.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mentioning מלכות means saying 'מלך העולם' or a similar phrase. The next step will ask what is new about this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Who is good and does good,' the fourth ברכה of ברכת המזון
It needs a mention of ה׳'s kingship

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbah bar bar Chana said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
'Who is good and does good' requires kingship.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about מלכות in הטוב והמטיב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברכה of הטוב והמטיב must contain a mention of מלכות.

steps.title: Didn't רבי יוחנן already say this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what is new, since רבי יוחנן already said that every ברכה needs מלכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? That any ברכה without kingship is not a ברכה? But רבי יוחנן already said that once!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the statement as repetitive. רבי יוחנן already taught a general rule that every ברכה needs מלכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every ברכה needs מלכות, then הטוב והמטיב is already included. So why say it again? The statement must be teaching something extra.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us (that is new)?
It is not called a ברכה

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
That any blessing that has no kingship
is not called a blessing?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אַמְרַהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן חֲדָא זִימְנָא!
phrases.english: But Rabbi Yochanan already said it once!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 39 as redundant.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's statement about הטוב והמטיב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן's general rule already requires מלכות in every ברכה, so this specific statement seems to add nothing.

steps.title: Two mentions of kingship
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains that הטוב והמטיב needs two mentions of מלכות: one for itself and one for בונה ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: It teaches that it needs two mentions of kingship, one for itself and one for 'Who builds Jerusalem.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers that the new point is a second mention of מלכות. הטוב והמטיב also makes up for בונה ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule only requires one מלכות per ברכה. The new point is that הטוב והמטיב carries an extra מלכות on behalf of the ברכה of בונה ירושלים. That ברכה is not said with its own full mention of ה׳'s kingship.
steps.whatToRemember: הטוב והמטיב has an extra mention of מלכות. One is its own, and one makes up for בונה ירושלים.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי זירא is not saying that בונה ירושלים itself must now add מלכות. The extra mention goes inside הטוב והמטיב.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
It comes to say that it requires two mentions of kingship,
one for itself
and one for 'Who builds Jerusalem.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the redundancy challenge of step 40.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the statement teaches an additional requirement, not the general rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The statement seemed to repeat the general rule that every ברכה needs one מלכות.
steps.terutzMaskana: הטוב והמטיב needs two מלכיות: its own, and one making up for בונה ירושלים.

steps.title: Then it should need three mentions
steps.stepSummary: If הטוב והמטיב makes up for the missing מלכות in בונה ירושלים, it should also make up for ברכת הארץ, for a total of three.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it should need three: one for itself, one for 'Who builds Jerusalem,' and one for the blessing of the land!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי זירא's answer. If one ברכה can make up for a missing מלכות in another, why stop at two?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא said הטוב והמטיב mentions מלכות twice: once for itself and once to make up for בונה ירושלים. But ברכת הארץ, the second ברכה, also has no מלכות. By the same logic it should be made up too, which would mean three mentions.

keyTerms.meaning: The blessing of the land (the second ברכה of ברכת המזון)

phrases.english: If so, it should need three:
one of its own,
and one for 'Who builds Jerusalem,'
and one for the blessing of the land!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי זירא's answer in Step 41
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's claim that הטוב והמטיב needs exactly two mentions of מלכות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ברכת הארץ also lacks מלכות, so the same make-up logic should produce three mentions, not two.

steps.title: Then בונה ירושלים should not need מלכות either
steps.stepSummary: ברכת הארץ has no מלכות because it is attached to the ברכה before it. The same is true of בונה ירושלים, so it should not need any make-up mention.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, why does the blessing of the land have no kingship? Because it is a blessing attached to the one before it. Then 'Who builds Jerusalem' should also not need it, since it too is attached to the one before it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question about ברכת הארץ. That answer then turns into a stronger challenge: בונה ירושלים should not need מלכות at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברכה that directly follows another ברכה does not need its own opening 'ברוך... מלך העולם.' That rule explains why ברכת הארץ needs no make-up. But בונה ירושלים is also a follow-on ברכה, so it should need no make-up either, and the second mention in הטוב והמטיב becomes unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברכה attached to (directly following) another ברכה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'סמוכה' means the ברכה is short. It means it follows right after another ברכה, so the opening of the first one carries over to it.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בִּרְכַּת הָאָרֶץ מַאי טַעְמָא לָא?
phrases.english: Rather, the blessing of the land, what is the reason it does not need it?
Because it is
a blessing juxtaposed to the one before it,
then 'Who builds Jerusalem' should also not need it,
since it is a blessing juxtaposed to the one before it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בִּרְכַּת הָאָרֶץ מַאי טַעְמָא לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains away the three-mentions problem, then turns the same reasoning into a stronger challenge
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for any make-up מלכות for בונה ירושלים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'attached ברכה' rule that excuses ברכת הארץ applies equally to בונה ירושלים.

steps.title: It is proper because the kingdom of David is mentioned
steps.stepSummary: בונה ירושלים truly does not need מלכות. But since it mentions the kingdom of דוד, it is only proper to also mention the kingdom of Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same is true: even 'Who builds Jerusalem' does not need it. But since one mentioned the kingdom of the house of David, it is not proper not to mention the kingdom of Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא agrees with the challenge on the basic rule. It then gives a separate reason why the extra mention of מלכות is still said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Strictly speaking, בונה ירושלים is an attached ברכה and needs no מלכות. But it speaks of the kingship of דוד's house. It would be disrespectful to mention a human kingdom without mentioning God's kingdom, so the extra mention is added in הטוב והמטיב.

keyTerms.meaning: The kingdom of the house of David

phrases.english: The same is true, that even
'Who builds Jerusalem' also does not need it.
But since he mentioned the kingdom of the house of David,
it is not proper
that he not mention the kingdom of Heaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 43
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concedes the basic rule but adds a separate reason (respect)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra mention exists because בונה ירושלים technically requires מלכות
steps.terutzMaskana: בונה ירושלים does not require it, but mentioning דוד's kingdom makes it proper to mention God's kingdom

steps.title: רב פפא: two besides its own
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא reads רבי זירא differently. הטוב והמטיב needs two mentions of מלכות besides its own, one for בונה ירושלים and one for ברכת הארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: This is what he means: it needs two kingships besides its own.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a different answer. He accepts the 'three mentions' idea by reading רבי זירא's 'two' as two in addition to its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer kept the total at two. רב פפא instead says the count is three: its own, plus one each for בונה ירושלים and ברכת הארץ. In his view, the challenge of Step 42 was simply correct.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two approaches. One says בונה ירושלים gets an extra mention only out of respect, because דוד's kingdom is mentioned there. רב פפא says הטוב והמטיב has three mentions of מלכות: its own, plus one each for the two ברכות before it.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: this is what he means:
it requires two kingships besides its own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternative answer to the challenge in Step 42
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Two' means two in addition to its own, three in total

steps.title: Forgot שבת in ברכת המזון
steps.stepSummary: In a scene in the study hall, רב גידל teaches רב הונא what to say if one forgot to mention שבת in ברכת המזון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא sat behind רב גידל, and רב גידל sat before רב הונא. He sat and said: If one erred and did not mention שבת, he says: 'Blessed is He Who gave Sabbaths for rest to His people Israel with love, as a sign and a covenant. Blessed is He Who sanctifies the Sabbath.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a story. It sets the scene and gives the ruling for someone who forgot שבת in ברכת המזון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fix is a short extra ברכה said after בונה ירושלים, so he does not have to start over. It mentions the Sabbath and closes with 'ברוך מקדש השבת.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the short ברכה we say today when one forgets רצה on שבת in ברכת המזון.

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַבִּי זֵירָא אֲחוֹרֵי דְּרַב גִּידֵּל,
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira sat behind Rav Giddel,

phrases.aramaic: וְיָתֵיב רַב גִּידֵּל קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא,
phrases.english: and Rav Giddel sat in front of Rav Huna,
and he sat and said:

phrases.aramaic: טָעָה וְלֹא הִזְכִּיר שֶׁל שַׁבָּת, אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: If one erred and did not mention Shabbat, he says:
'Blessed is He Who gave Sabbaths for rest
to His people Israel with love,
as a sign and a covenant,
Blessed is He Who sanctifies the Sabbath.'

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַבִּי זֵירָא אֲחוֹרֵי דְּרַב גִּידֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic, about forgetting שבת in ברכת המזון
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who forgot שבת in ברכת המזון says a short ברכה ending 'ברוך מקדש השבת.'

steps.title: Who said it? רב
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא asks who taught this ruling, and רב גידל answers: רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Who said it? רב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא asks for the source of the ruling, and רב גידל names רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a challenge. It simply identifies the source. Naming רב as the source tells us whose authority the ruling rests on.

phrases.english: He said to him: Who said it?
Rav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ruling in Step 46
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is the authority behind the שבת ruling

steps.title: Forgot יום טוב in ברכת המזון
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל teaches what to say if one forgot to mention יום טוב in ברכת המזון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Again he sat and said: If one erred and did not mention יום טוב, he says: 'Blessed is He Who gave festivals to His people Israel for joy and remembrance. Blessed is He Who sanctifies Israel and the seasons.'
steps.whatsHappening: Using the same pattern, רב גידל now gives the short ברכה for someone who forgot יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברכה matches the one for שבת, but the wording fits יום טוב: 'for joy and remembrance.' It closes with 'מקדש ישראל והזמנים,' because Israel sets the dates of the festivals.

keyTerms.meaning: Who sanctifies Israel and the seasons

phrases.english: Again he sat and said:

phrases.aramaic: טָעָה וְלֹא הִזְכִּיר שֶׁל יוֹם טוֹב, אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: If one erred and did not mention the Festival, he says:
'Blessed is He Who gave festivals
to His people Israel for joy and for remembrance,
Blessed is He Who sanctifies Israel and the seasons.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel ruling to Step 46, for יום טוב
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who forgot יום טוב in ברכת המזון says a short ברכה ending 'ברוך מקדש ישראל והזמנים.'

steps.title: Again: who said it? רב
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא again asks who taught this, and רב גידל again answers: רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Who said it? רב.
steps.whatsHappening: Exactly as before, רב הונא asks for the source and is told it is רב. The story continues on the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The repeated question and answer shows the same pattern a second time. It confirms that both rulings come from רב. The repetition sets up what follows in the story.

phrases.english: He said to him: Who said it?
Rav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ruling in Step 48, mirroring Step 47
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is the authority behind the יום טוב ruling

steps.title: What to say if one forgot ראש חודש in ברכת המזון
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל teaches that if someone forgot to mention ראש חודש in ברכת המזון, he says a short make-up blessing about ראש חודש being given for remembrance.
steps.simpleTranslation: Again he sat and said: If someone made a mistake and did not mention ראש חודש, he says: "Blessed is He Who gave ראשי חדשים to His people ישראל for remembrance."
steps.whatsHappening: רב גידל gives a third make-up formula. This one is for a person who forgot ראש חודש in ברכת המזון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as the earlier rulings for שבת and יום טוב. The wording is fitted to ראש חודש: it is given "לזכרון," for remembrance. Notice that, unlike the יום טוב formula, the word "joy" (שמחה) is not mentioned here.

keyTerms.meaning: He sat again; he went back and taught once more
The New Moon, the first day of a Jewish month

phrases.english: Again he sat and said:
phrases.notes: רב גידל, continuing the same scene

phrases.aramaic: טָעָה וְלֹא הִזְכִּיר שֶׁל רֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ
phrases.english: If one erred and did not mention that of the New Moon,
he says: "Blessed is He Who gave New Moons
to His people Israel for remembrance."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third ruling in the series, after שבת (step 46) and יום טוב (step 48).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who forgot ראש חודש in ברכת המזון says: "ברוך שנתן ראשי חדשים לעמו ישראל לזכרון."

steps.title: The reporter is unsure about the details of the ראש חודש ruling
steps.stepSummary: The one telling the story, רבי זירא, admits he does not remember three things: whether "joy" was mentioned, whether there was a closing blessing, and whether this ruling came from רב גידל himself or from his teacher רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And I do not know whether he said 'joy' in it or did not say 'joy' in it, whether he closed it with a blessing or did not close it with a blessing, and whether it was his own teaching or his teacher's."
steps.whatsHappening: The reporter of the story says honestly that he is unsure about three details of the ראש חודש ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שבת and יום טוב, רב הונא asked who taught the ruling, and the answer was clear: רב. Here there is no such clear answer. The reporter does not know whether the word שמחה belongs in the formula, whether it ends with a closing "ברוך אתה ה׳" (חתימה) like the others, or whether the ruling comes from רב גידל or from רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Closes, meaning ends with a concluding blessing formula

steps.confusionAlert: The speaker here is not רב גידל. It is the one reporting the scene, often identified as רבי זירא, who is unsure what רב גידל said.

phrases.english: And I do not know
phrases.notes: This is the person telling the story speaking.

phrases.english: whether he said "joy" in it
or did not say "joy" in it,

phrases.aramaic: אִי חָתֵים בָּהּ, אִי לָא חָתֵים בָּהּ,
phrases.english: whether he concluded it with a blessing or did not conclude it with a blessing,
and whether it was his own or his teacher's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies step 50 by admitting uncertainty about its exact wording, its ending, and its source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The reporter cannot confirm three details of the ראש חודש formula: mention of שמחה, a closing חתימה, or attribution to רב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This open uncertainty prepares the ground for later discussion about how the ראש חודש make-up formula differs from those of שבת and יום טוב.

steps.title: A new story begins: רב נחמן makes a mistake
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new story. גידל בר מניומי was standing before רב נחמן, and רב נחמן made a mistake in ברכת המזון.
steps.simpleTranslation: גידל בר מניומי was standing before רב נחמן, and רב נחמן made a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new story. Here it only gives the scene and says that רב נחמן made a mistake; what happened next comes in the following lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic stays the same, forgetting the special day's mention in ברכת המזון, but now it is told through a real-life case. On one reading, רב נחמן forgot to mention שבת. The story will show what happened in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, a student present before רב נחמן
Was standing before him, attending him as a student

phrases.english: Giddel bar Manyumi was standing
before Rav Nachman;
Rav Nachman erred
phrases.notes: He forgot the special mention, which the story will continue to describe

steps.triggerLanguage: גִּידֵּל בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי הֲוָה קָאֵי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from taught rulings to a practical story on the same topic of forgetting the special mention in ברכת המזון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup only: רב נחמן erred in ברכת המזון while גידל בר מניומי was present.
